data.description:
## Observed

While attributing bug `ff4a-2832-def4-4e55`, `link_tickets(ff4a…, d80d-7be7-1c0a-4231, "caused_by")`
routed through the **MCP server** was refused:

```
Error: cannot create caused_by link — target ticket 'd80d-7be7-1c0a-4231' has no commit
referencing it, so it cannot be shown to have introduced anything.
```

The claim is false. Commit `44ec1c2e67373a2e2b888a1beb0bf1cb7b0f6d39` has the subject
`d80d-7be7-1c0a-4231: async gate start (P2)`, and locally:

```
$ rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev 44ec1c2e6737
verify-commit-ticket: OK - resolved d80d-7be7-1c0a-4231
```

Running the identical `rebar link` from a local worktree with full history **succeeded
immediately**.

## Likely mechanism (not root-caused; filed as discovered work)

`caused_by_refusal` (`src/rebar/_commands/link_revert.py:30`) calls
`commit_impact.referencing_commits({target}, tracker, code_root)`. Through the MCP server
`code_root` is the container's `REBAR_ROOT=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code` clone, which the mcp
service entrypoint creates **blobless and single-branch** in the background
(`infra/compose/docker-compose.yml`, `MCP_CODE_DIR`). If that clone is shallow, lagging, or
mid-clone, the scan finds nothing.

The guard is explicitly written to distinguish "no commit" from "this checkout has no history"
— `referencing_commits` returning `None` (unreadable history) **allows** the link. But a clone
that reads fine and simply does not **contain** the commit returns an empty set, which is
indistinguishable from a genuinely commit-less target. The guard's own stated intent is
therefore defeated by a partial checkout rather than an absent one.

## Why it matters

The refusal message names `--force="<reason>"` as the remedy. Agents are prohibited from using
force overrides (`AGENTS.md`), so a correct, evidence-backed attribution becomes unrecordable
through the sanctioned surface — the exact "pushes toward `--force`" failure mode that
`ff4a-2832-def4-4e55` raises about the plan-review gate. The likely real-world outcome is a
silently **unattributed** bug close, which corrupts the escaped-defect lenses the edge exists
to feed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 - The mechanism is confirmed: establish whether the MCP container's code clone can
      resolve an arbitrary historical `main` commit, and whether depth/lag/in-progress-clone is
      the cause.
- [ ] AC2 - A `caused_by` target whose commit exists on `main` but is not present in the scanning
      checkout is NOT refused as "has no commit". Distinguish "this checkout cannot see that
      commit" from "no such commit exists", the way the guard already distinguishes an unreadable
      history.
- [ ] AC3 - Defect-seeded test: a link whose target is referenced by a commit absent from the
      scanning clone but present upstream must not be refused.

## Non-goals

Not removing the `caused_by` commit guard — refusing a genuinely commit-less target is correct
and deliberate.
data.title: caused_by links are refused through the MCP server because its code clone cannot resolve the referencing commit, pushing agents toward --force
